  WHY: A tag refspec reaches the undefined call and raises `NameError`, causing the hook to emit a traceback and block the push instead of skipping a tag-only write.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: _evaluate_bash guarded-subcommand gate (lines ~1730-1745 of the new file) and guard_targets reserved-word loop (lines ~850-870 of the new file) | severity=high | confidence=[4]

  PROBLEM: For `time -p git push`, `guard_targets` can return no targets while a guarded Git subcommand is detected, and `_evaluate_bash` silently returns without checking the push.
  WHY: This allows a push from a session checkout on a merged branch to proceed without a guard check or warning.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_push_refspec_targets (added by this PR, around line 596 of the new file) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: `_push_refspec_targets` calls `_refspec_writes_no_branch(spec)`, which is not defined in the root copy.
  WHY: Tag refspecs raise `NameError`; the hook prints a traceback and blocks the push instead of skipping the tag-only write. The same finding was reported twice under CORRECTNESS & LOGIC and ERROR PATHS & EDGE CASES.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: For `time -p git push`, `guard_targets` returns no targets while `_evaluate_bash` detects a guarded subcommand, then silently returns without checking the push.
  WHY: A push from a session checkout on a merged branch can proceed without the check or warning.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "The root `.claude/` copy lands through a `[claude-twin-sync]` commit, so `test_template_copies_are_identical` stays red until then." (PR description, Evidence section). Expected change site: .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py. Evidence of absence: The root copy (1769 lines) is missing several functions and features present in the twin copy (1856 lines) that this PR's intent requires. Concretely, the root copy's diff does not add: `_refspec_writes_no_branch` (defined in the twin, called but not defined in the root — see the BLOCKER above); `_tilde_word_flags` (the twin uses it to keep tilde quoting per occurrence; the root uses only the per-text `_literal_tilde_words` frozenset, so `git -C ~/wt commit -m "~/wt"; git -C ~/wt push origin HEAD:feature/x` misjudges the push's directory); `_COMMAND_RESERVED_WORD_PREFIXES`, `_COMPOUND_OPENING_WORDS`, `_COMPOUND_CLOSING_WORDS` (the root copy's guard_targets does not skip reserved words and does not track compound depth, so `then git push …`, `do git commit …`, `! git …`, `time git …` are unguarded and `if true; then cd wt; fi; git push …` follows the inner `cd` even though the body may not run). The PR modifies the root copy to an intermediate state that is neither the pre-PR code nor the twin; the `[claude-twin-sync]` follow-up will close the gap, but until that commit lands the interactive session runs a broken hook. Severity: BLOCKER. ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5.
